experiment: E224 Amendment 1 (rl_67m, cell P2.41 runs 6-7): the plural task becomes balanced number agreement; the W0 bands become readings, with one W0 stop on the regime
amends: experiments/rl_67m/results/predictions_E224.json (unchanged, as filed); run_newtasks.py and read_newtasks.py read both, this file's thresholds over the original's
filed: 2026-11-20, after the rehearsal ctl (cluster job 62147, log cluster/logs/commute-rl67m-nt-62147.out) and before any arm, null or reading job. Asked by the coordinator the same day

why.W0 bands: the filed bands were guesses from task#2191's 30 curated items; the mined and filled Pile items are noisier and two of the bands missed (plural top-1 0.19 and top-5 0.70, sequence top-5 0.694). They were never stops in the code; they are now recorded readings
why.plural: the 5-step RL rehearsal in job 62147 took plural top-1 from 0.17 to 1.000 at KL 1.69 and the cue-removed control from 0.12 to 0.998: RL learned 'say they/their/them' everywhere, not agreement. With half the items singular, the reward needs the pronoun's number to follow the antecedent's

changes.plural task: rl_tasks_2191.agreement_items: mined as before (same rows, gap 32, the det inside the window, nothing between but non-pronoun tokens and no newline), now for both numbers. A cue is a pronoun token whose nearest antecedent-shaped bigram before it has the pronoun's number: plural '<DET_PL> <noun>s' (noun not ss/us/is, singular form one token) before they/their/them; singular '<DET_SG> <noun>' (DET_SG: the, this, a, an, each, every; noun not ending in s, plural form one token) before he/she/it/his/her/its/him. Any pronoun of either number or case between ends the scan. At most one item of each number per row; each number filled to n // 2, then both cut to the smaller count (balance by subsampling) and interleaved plural first, so every prefix the reads take is balanced
changes.plural sets: target = the agreeing number's set (they/their/them, or he/she/it/his/her/its/him, each with and without a leading space where one token); competitor = the other number's set (' a' and ' the' are no longer competitors). Reward = the sampled token is in the agreeing set; per-row contrast = log p(agreeing set) - log p(other number's set)
changes.plural control: unchanged in kind: the antecedent's number swapped in the same window (these <-> this, those -> that, other determiners -> the; the noun's other-number form); read on the item's agreeing set
changes.held_read: adds top-1 on the plural-antecedent and singular-antecedent halves apart (top1_plural, top1_singular), recorded, not a gate
changes.W0: the filed W0 bands are readings, not stops. One W0 stop in ctl: for plural and sequence, W0 held-out top-5 minus the anchor's (addition) top-5 is at least regime_min_se standard errors of the difference (sqrt(se_a^2 + se_b^2), 1,024 items each). Reference 62147: sequence 0.694 - 0.308 = 0.387 against 2 se = 0.041; plural (old task) 0.394 against 0.041
changes.unchanged: every other setting, threshold, gate (learned, stable null), arm, reading and rule of predictions_E224.json

expected.item counts: set by the CPU dry run of this code before the ctl rerun (reports/plans/2026-11-19_plan_rl-67m.md, Stage 2c/3c, Amendment 1)
expected.W0 plural (balanced): top-1 0.15-0.55, top-5 0.6-1.0, contrast -1.5 to +1.5; the singular half's top-1 likely above the plural half's (the 67M writes 'it' often)
expected.regime: passes on both (sequence 0.39 over the anchor in 62147; plural above 0.2)
expected.RL seed 0 at the target: the 62147 rehearsal says RL moves plural fast; with balanced items a policy that always writes one number reads top-1 about 0.5 overall, so top1_plural and top1_singular are recorded beside the gate

edge_cases.fewer singular than plural items (or the: both cut to the smaller count; under min_items (1,000) held-out the ctl stops naming the task
edge_cases.the anchor's own row in the regime: not read (only plural and sequence are compared to it)
